newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to replace CRP oil holding with new firm.
newsitem.headline: Romania to replace CRP oil holding with new firm.

text.p: Romania will replace its National Oil Company (CRP) holding with a new firm which it hopes will streamline the oil sector and ensure a smooth cash flow, a senior official said on Friday.

The weekly Adevarul Economic business newspaper quoted State Secretary Liviu Luca as saying the new company would group the Petrom oil company, three refineries and the Peco SA petroleum products retailer.
"The new company will help the oil sector solve the problems related to financial bottlenecks and will also ensure a smooth cash flow in the sector," Luca said.
The move is part of the new centrist government's drive to restructure oversized industries and close loss-making firms.
Last month, the government decreed to dissolve the CRP starting July 1 and replace it with a more efficient structure.
The CRP holding now groups the country's 10 refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as a research institute and an oil exploration company.

Luca said the refineries expected to be included in the new company were Petrobrazi SA, in the oilfield of Ploiesti, Rafo Onesti, which processes the crude oil extracted in the Moldova region and Arpechim, in the southern city of Pitesti.
"The new company will be involved solely in commercial activities," Luca said.

When CRP was created in 1995, authorities believed they could provide funds to import crude oil badly needed by Romania's industrial and energy sectors as well as streamline the exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
But CRP officials admitted recently that the initial plan had failed to "function properly" and that a new structure was needed to replace the holding.
Luca said the CRP was saddled with debts amounting to $500 million, following a sharp depreciation of the national leu currency in January and due to high interest rates on credits.
"As a result of these debts, foreign investors are reluctant to buy refineries. Who is going to pay, let's say, one million dollars for a refinery and another million to take over its debts?"
Romania's crude oil output amounted to some 6.8 million tonnes last year.
Romania's refining industry, with a capacity of 34 million tonnes and developed during the rule of late dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, is the largest in central and eastern Europe.
